gloss.c.shrink.b: A shop loses a lot through broken products, old products and theft. Help to keep it low. A broken or damaged product? Do not put it back: write it off the way your shop does it. Your own shopping: pay at the till like every customer, and keep the receipt. In many shops you may not ring up your own shopping: a colleague does it. Never eat or take a product without paying, not even a small one. Some shops check bags: that is a shop rule, not a sign of distrust in you. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.shrink.p: I pay first, and I keep the receipt.
gloss.c.shrink.s: At the end of your shift you are hungry. A sandwich is past its date today. What do you do?
gloss.c.shrink.o1: Ask the manager what the rule is.
gloss.c.shrink.o2: Eat it: it is thrown away anyway.
gloss.c.shrink.o3: Take it home in your bag.
gloss.c.shrink.w: In many shops, taking a product without paying is stealing, also when it is old. Asking first keeps you safe.
gloss.w.kasverschil: the cash difference (more or less money in the till than there should be)
gloss.w.kluis: the safe (a strong box for money)
gloss.w.overval: the robbery (someone takes money with threats)
gloss.s.shopclose.2: We count the till with two people.
gloss.c.shopclose.a: Sorry, we are closed. Tomorrow we open at eight.
gloss.c.shopclose: A robbery: give it, and stay safe
gloss.c.shopclose.b: At closing time there is a lot of money in the till, so shops have rules: count it with two people, take the money to the safe, and lock the back door first. A robbery (overval)? Your life is worth more than the money. Stay calm, do what they say, and do not fight or run after them. Remember what you can: clothes, height, voice. When they are gone: lock the door, call 112, and touch nothing. Afterwards, talk about it with your manager or someone you trust. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.shopclose.p: We are closing. I am locking the door.
gloss.c.shopclose.s: A man with a knife wants the money from your till. What do you do?
gloss.c.shopclose.o1: Stay calm, and give him the money.
gloss.c.shopclose.o2: Fight him: the money is not his.
gloss.c.shopclose.o3: Run to the back, and lock yourself in.
gloss.c.shopclose.w: Fighting or running makes a robber nervous and more dangerous. Money can be replaced. You cannot.
gloss.w.inlener: the hirer (the company where the agency sends you to work)
gloss.w.vestiging: the branch (the office of the agency in your town)
gloss.w.intakegesprek: the intake interview (the first talk at the agency)
gloss.w.opstapplaats: the pick-up point (where the agency’s bus picks you up)
gloss.w.bedrijfsregels: the company rules (the rules of the hirer)
gloss.w.aanspreekpunt: the contact person (the person you go to with questions)
gloss.s.hirer.1: Tomorrow you work at a new hirer.
gloss.s.hirer.2: Who is my contact person here?
gloss.s.hirer.3: The bus leaves the pick-up point at six.
gloss.c.hirer.q: Can you start at a new hirer tomorrow?
gloss.c.hirer.a: Yes. What time must I be there?
gloss.c.hirer.b: You work through an agency (uitzendbureau), but you do the work at another company: the hirer (inlener). The agency is your employer: your contract, your pay, your payslip and your days off come from the agency. The hirer tells you what to do on the work floor, and must keep your work safe, just like for its own workers. Report sick the way your agency says: often to the agency and to the hirer. Keep the name and phone number of your contact person at the agency in your phone. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.hirer.p: Who is my contact person at the agency?
gloss.c.hirer.s: At the hirer you must work with a machine. Nobody showed you how. What do you do?
gloss.c.hirer.o1: Ask the hirer to show you first.
gloss.c.hirer.o2: Try it: the agency is responsible.
gloss.c.hirer.w: The hirer must show you how to work safely, the same as its own workers. Asking for it is your right.
gloss.w.fase: the phase (a step in your agency contract: A, B or C)
gloss.w.uitzendbeding: the agency clause (your work can stop when the hirer no longer needs you)
gloss.w.aflopen: to end, to run out (a contract)
gloss.w.doorwerken: to keep working (at the same place)
gloss.w.vastecontract: the permanent contract (a contract without an end date)
gloss.w.onderbreking: the break (a time without work between two contracts)
gloss.s.phases.1: Which phase am I in now?
gloss.c.phases.a: Okay. Do you have other work for me?
gloss.c.phases.b: Most agency workers work under a cao for agency workers (uitzend-cao). It has phases. In phase A, your work can usually stop when the hirer no longer needs you (uitzendbeding). In phase B, you get contracts for a fixed time. In phase C, you get a permanent contract with the agency. How long each phase lasts is in your cao. Ask the agency which phase you are in, and keep all your contracts. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.phases.p: How long does phase A last for me?
gloss.c.phases.s: You worked a long time for the same agency. You still get short contracts. What do you do?
gloss.c.phases.o1: Ask the agency which phase you are in.
gloss.c.phases.o2: Nothing: agency work is always short.
gloss.c.phases.o3: Stop, and look for another agency.
gloss.c.phases.w: After enough time, the cao gives you more security. The agency can tell you where you are, and the union can check it with you.
gloss.w.inhouding: the deduction (money taken off your pay)
gloss.w.vastekracht: the permanent worker (a worker employed by the hirer itself)
gloss.w.vervoer: the transport (the bus or van to work)
gloss.w.schriftelijk: in writing (on paper or in an email)
gloss.w.navragen: to check, to ask about (to find out if something is right)
gloss.w.brutoloon: the gross pay (your pay before tax and deductions)
gloss.s.deductions.1: What is this deduction on my payslip?
gloss.s.deductions.2: Do I earn the same as the permanent workers?
gloss.s.deductions.3: I want to see that on paper first.
gloss.c.deductions.q: We take the cost of the bus off your pay.
gloss.c.deductions.a: Is that allowed? I will check that first.
gloss.c.deductions: What may come off your pay?
gloss.c.deductions.b: You have a right to at least the same pay as workers of the hirer who do the same work. Money that is taken off your pay (inhouding) must be on your payslip. Tax and premiums come off by law. Apart from those, the agency may only take off two costs from the minimum wage: rent for your housing and the premium for health insurance, and only if you agreed to it in writing. Other costs, like transport, work clothes, fines or a fee for finding you a job, may not come off the minimum wage. Do not understand a deduction? Ask the agency to explain it in writing. General information. For your situation: ask the union, the Juridisch Loket or FairWork.
gloss.c.deductions.s: The agency takes money off your pay for the bus to work. You earn the minimum wage. What do you do?
gloss.c.deductions.o1: Ask about it: this is not allowed.
gloss.c.deductions.o2: Nothing: you take the bus every day.
gloss.c.deductions.o3: Stop taking the bus, and walk.
gloss.c.deductions.w: From the minimum wage, only rent and health insurance may come off, and only with your written yes. The union or the Juridisch Loket can help you.
gloss.w.huisvesting: the housing (a place to live, arranged by the agency)
gloss.w.huisgenoot: the housemate (a person who lives in the same house)
gloss.w.huisregels: the house rules (the rules of the house where you live)
gloss.w.huismeester: the housing manager (the person who looks after the house)
gloss.w.meldpunt: the reporting point (a place where you can report a problem)
gloss.s.agencyhome.1: I want my own rental contract.
gloss.s.agencyhome.2: There is mould in the bathroom.
gloss.s.agencyhome.3: I am calling the union for advice.
gloss.c.agencyhome.q: You must leave the house on Friday.
gloss.c.agencyhome.a: That is very short. I will ask for advice first.
gloss.c.agencyhome: Your home, and where to get help
gloss.c.agencyhome.b: Does the agency arrange your housing? Then you get a rental contract of your own, in writing, apart from your work contract. Keep a copy. It says what you pay, and how and when the rental ends. Your work stops? Your home does not always stop on the same day: ask for advice before you leave. Unsafe or very full housing, threats, or pay that is too low? Get help: the union, the Juridisch Loket (free legal advice), FairWork, or the Nederlandse Arbeidsinspectie, where you can also report anonymously. General information. For your situation: ask the union, the Juridisch Loket or FairWork.
gloss.c.agencyhome.p: May I have a copy of my rental contract?
gloss.c.agencyhome.s: Your work stops. The housing manager says you must leave the house today. What do you do?
gloss.c.agencyhome.o1: Ask the union or Juridisch Loket first.
gloss.c.agencyhome.o2: Leave today, and sleep at a friend’s.
gloss.c.agencyhome.o3: Pack your bag, and sleep outside.
gloss.c.agencyhome.w: Your rental contract has its own rules, apart from your work. Advice helps you know when you really must leave.
gloss.w.advertentie: the ad (a text that offers a job or a thing)
gloss.w.eis: the requirement (what you must have or can do)
gloss.w.contactpersoon: the contact person (the person you can call or write to)
gloss.s.vacancy.1: I saw your ad on the internet.
gloss.s.vacancy.2: Is the job part-time or full-time?
gloss.c.vacancy.a: I am calling about your vacancy. Is it still open?
gloss.c.vacancy: Call, or send a short message
gloss.c.vacancy.b: Read the ad well: the hours, the place, and what you must have, like a driving licence or a certificate. You do not need to have everything: if you have most of it, try anyway. Call or write a short message: say your name, which job, and why you want it. Never pay money to get a job, and never send your login codes for an ad.
gloss.c.vacancy.p: I have no diploma, but I do have a lot of experience.
gloss.c.vacancy.s: An ad asks for 3 years of experience. You have 2 years. What do you do?
gloss.c.vacancy.o1: Apply anyway, and say what you can do.
gloss.c.vacancy.o2: Do not apply: you have too little.
gloss.c.vacancy.w: An ad often asks for more than the job really needs. Being honest about what you can do works better than lying.
gloss.w.afwijzing: the rejection (you did not get the job)
gloss.w.aanbod: the offer (they offer you the job)
gloss.w.proefdag: the trial day (one day of work, to try)
gloss.w.nabellen: to call back (to ask how it is going)
gloss.c.result.q: Unfortunately, we are choosing someone else.
gloss.c.result.a: Too bad. May I ask why?
gloss.c.result: A no is not the end
gloss.c.result.b: Heard nothing after a week? You may call back and ask politely. Got a no? Ask what you can do better next time: many employers tell you. Then try again: most people get a few no’s first. Got a yes? Ask when you start, and ask for your contract before you begin. Invited for a trial day? Ask before how long it is, and if it is paid.
gloss.c.result.p: What can I do better next time?
gloss.c.result.s: After a job interview, you get a no by e-mail. What do you do?
gloss.c.result.o1: Ask politely what you can do better.
gloss.c.result.o2: Write back that they made a mistake.
gloss.c.result.o3: Stop applying: it does not work.
gloss.c.result.w: Feedback helps you in your next interview. A polite question also leaves a good picture of you.
gloss.w.verloopdatum: the expiry date (the last day it is valid)
gloss.w.volgnummer: the queue number (the ticket with your turn)
gloss.s.residence.1: My residence permit is valid for one more year.
gloss.s.residence.2: What is the expiry date of your passport?
gloss.s.residence.3: I have an appointment at the town hall.
gloss.c.residence.q: Your residence permit has almost expired.
gloss.c.residence.a: Then I will apply for a new one right away.
gloss.c.residence.b: From the EU? Then you may live and work here with a valid passport or ID card: you do not need a permit. From outside the EU? Then you need a valid residence permit. On the card it says if you may work. Check the expiry date of your papers. Apply for a new permit at the IND in time: months before the date, not in the last week. Keep a copy of every letter. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.residence.p: My permit expires soon. What must I do?
gloss.c.residence.s: Your residence permit expires in two months. You are very busy at work. What do you do?
gloss.c.residence.o1: Apply for a new one now.
gloss.c.residence.w: Without a valid permit, you may not be allowed to work. A new permit takes time, so you start early.
gloss.w.meterstand: the meter reading (the numbers on the meter for gas, power or water)
gloss.w.naambordje: the name sign (your name at the door)
gloss.w.woning: the home (a house or a flat)
gloss.w.doorsturen: to forward (send on to a new address)
gloss.s.newhome.2: My name is not on the letterbox.
gloss.s.newhome.3: I am passing on my new address.
gloss.c.newhome.a: In a new home. Here is my new address.
gloss.c.newhome.b: Moving? Tell the gemeente your new address quickly: you must do that. Also tell your employer, your bank, your insurance and your doctor. Put your name on the letterbox, or letters do not reach you. On moving day, write down the meter readings and take photos of them. Then you only pay for what you used.
gloss.c.newhome.p: I have moved. This is my new address.
gloss.c.newhome.s: You moved two weeks ago. Your letters still go to your old address. What do you do?
gloss.c.newhome.o1: Give your new address to the gemeente now.
gloss.c.newhome.o2: Wait: the post will find you.
gloss.c.newhome.o3: Ask your old neighbour to keep your letters.
gloss.c.newhome.w: Important letters, like fines or tax letters, have dates. When they go to the wrong address, you can miss them.
gloss.w.pensioen: the pension (money for when you are old)
gloss.w.periode: the period (the weeks or the month of this pay)
gloss.w.afkorting: the abbreviation (a short form of a word)
gloss.w.personeelsnummer: the staff number (your number at the company)
gloss.s.payparts.2: This amount goes to my pension.
gloss.s.payparts.3: Which period is this pay for?
gloss.c.payparts.a: It is at the top, next to my name.
gloss.c.payparts.b: Your payslip has many lines and short words. At the top: your name, your staff number and the period. Then your gross pay, your hours and any extra pay. Then what comes off: tax and premiums. In many jobs, you and your employer both pay for your pension: you see your part on your payslip. At the bottom: your net pay. Do not understand a line? Ask your employer to explain it. Keep all your payslips. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.payparts.p: What does this line on my payslip mean?
gloss.c.payparts.s: On your payslip, money goes to "pensioen". You do not know why. What do you do?
gloss.c.payparts.o1: Ask your employer to explain it.
gloss.c.payparts.o2: Ask to stop it, to get more money now.
gloss.c.payparts.o3: Ignore it: you will not stay that long.
gloss.c.payparts.w: Pension money is saved for you, for later. You usually keep it when you change jobs. Asking helps you know what is yours.
gloss.w.zwartwerken: to work off the books (no contract, no tax, no rights on paper)
gloss.w.voorschot: the advance (part of your pay before payday)
gloss.w.nabetaling: the back pay (money you get later, to correct your pay)
gloss.w.bankafschrift: the bank statement (a list of the money in and out)
gloss.s.latepay.2: I do not work off the books.
gloss.c.latepay.q: You will get the missing money next month.
gloss.c.latepay.a: Can I get that on paper?
gloss.c.latepay: Late or cash pay? Act in time
gloss.c.latepay.b: Your pay must come on the day in your contract or cao. Is it late, or is money missing? Ask about it in writing, for example in an e-mail. Keep your bank statements and your own list of hours. Paid in cash, without a payslip? Then it is often off the books (zwart): your hours are not registered, and later it is hard to prove your work or to get a benefit. Ask for a payslip. General information. For your situation: ask the union, the Juridisch Loket or FairWork.
gloss.c.latepay.p: My pay has not come in yet. When will it come?
gloss.c.latepay.s: Your boss says: "From now on I pay you in cash. No payslip, that is easier." What do you do?
gloss.c.latepay.o1: Say no, and ask for a payslip.
gloss.c.latepay.o2: Say yes: cash is more money.
gloss.c.latepay.o3: Say yes, but only this month.
gloss.c.latepay.w: Without a payslip, your work is not on paper. Then you can lose rights, for example to a benefit when you lose your job.
gloss.w.saldo: the balance (how many days you still have)
gloss.w.goedkeuren: to approve (to say yes to it)
gloss.w.verlopen: to expire (it is no longer valid)
gloss.w.drukte: the busy time (a lot of work)
gloss.w.aanvraag: the request (you ask for something, often on a form)
gloss.s.holiday.1: How many days off do I still have?
gloss.s.holiday.3: I am filling in the form.
gloss.c.holiday.q: In summer it is busy. Can you go on holiday in May?
gloss.c.holiday.a: I would rather go in July. Then my family is at home.
gloss.c.holiday: Your days off: use them in time
gloss.c.holiday.b: Check how many days off you still have: often it is on your payslip or in the app. Plan your holiday early, and ask in writing. Your legal days off expire 6 months after the end of the year, unless you could not take them. Extra days from your cao or contract stay valid longer, usually 5 years. Does your job end? Then you get money for the days you did not take. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.holiday.p: I want to take my days off this year.
gloss.c.holiday.s: It is November. You still have 12 days off from this year. Your supervisor says nothing about it. What do you do?
gloss.c.holiday.o1: Ask when you can take them.
gloss.c.holiday.o3: Forget them: they are gone now.
gloss.c.holiday.w: Days off are for rest, and they can expire. When you ask in time, you can still plan them.
gloss.w.geboorteverlof: the birth leave (for the partner, when a baby is born)
gloss.w.bijzonderverlof: the special leave (for example for a wedding or a funeral)
gloss.w.vrijvragen: to ask for a day off
gloss.s.special.1: My brother is getting married. Can I ask for a day off?
gloss.s.special.2: My uncle has died. The funeral is on Friday.
gloss.s.special.3: Do I have to work at Christmas?
gloss.c.special.q: Congratulations on your baby! Are you taking birth leave?
gloss.c.special.a: Yes, the first week I am at home.
gloss.c.special: A wedding, a funeral, a baby
gloss.c.special.b: Is your baby born, and are you the partner? Then you get 1 week of birth leave with pay, in the first 4 weeks. Your cao often gives special leave (bijzonder verlof) for your wedding, or for a funeral in your family. Public holidays, like Christmas: no law says you are free. Your contract or cao says if you are free, or if you get extra pay. Ask for your days off in time. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.special.p: My wife is having a baby. How do I ask for birth leave?
gloss.c.special.s: Your father has died abroad. You want to go to the funeral. What do you do?
gloss.c.special.o1: Tell your employer, and ask what leave you can get.
gloss.c.special.o2: Just go, and tell them when you are back.
gloss.c.special.o3: Do not go: you have no days off left.
gloss.c.special.w: Your employer understands that this is very important. Many cao’s give special leave, and you can also use your days off.
gloss.w.nietlekker: not well (you feel a bit sick)
gloss.w.uitzieken: to stay home until you are well
gloss.s.unwell.2: I have a headache and I have a cold.
gloss.s.unwell.3: I am going home. I am sick.
gloss.c.unwell.q: You look pale. Are you okay?
gloss.c.unwell.a: No, I do not feel well. May I go home?
gloss.c.unwell: Sick at work, or on holiday
gloss.c.unwell.b: Do you feel sick at work? Tell your supervisor before you go home: that is your sick report. Do not just leave. Did you get sick during your holiday? Report it to your employer the same way as at home, also from abroad. Then the sick days usually do not count as days off. You may need a note from a doctor there. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.unwell.s: You are on holiday in your home country. You get the flu and stay in bed for 5 days. What do you do?
gloss.c.unwell.o1: Report it to your employer right away.
gloss.c.unwell.o2: Nothing: you are on holiday anyway.
gloss.c.unwell.o3: Tell your employer when you are back.
gloss.c.unwell.w: When you report it in time, the sick days usually do not count as days off. Then you can still use those days later.
gloss.w.verklaring: the statement (what you write or say about what happened)
gloss.s.injury.1: I have had an accident at work.
gloss.c.injury.q: Will you write down your statement here?
gloss.c.injury.a: Yes. May I have a copy?
gloss.c.injury: Hurt at work: write it down
gloss.c.injury.b: Were you hurt at work? Write down what happened, when and where, and who saw it. Take photos, and keep all papers from the doctor. Ask for a copy of the accident report. Were you hurt because the work was not safe? Then your employer usually must pay for your damage. You do not have to prove that it was their fault: the employer must show they did enough for your safety. Ask for advice before you sign anything. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.injury.p: May I have a copy of the report?
gloss.c.injury.s: You hurt your hand at a machine without a guard. Later, your boss asks you to sign a paper: "It was my own fault." What do you do?
gloss.c.injury.o1: Do not sign it. Ask for advice first.
gloss.c.injury.o2: Sign it, so there are no problems.
gloss.c.injury.o3: Sign it, but keep a photo of it.
gloss.c.injury.w: What you sign can count later, for example when you ask for compensation. First get advice from the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.l.debt: A debt to the boss or the agency
gloss.w.tussenpersoon: the middleman (someone who arranges work for money)
gloss.w.rente: the interest (extra money you pay on a loan)
gloss.s.debt.1: I had to pay for this job.
gloss.s.debt.2: My debt gets higher every month.
gloss.c.debt.q: You may only leave when your debt is paid.
gloss.c.debt.a: That is not allowed. I am asking for help.
gloss.c.debt.b: In the Netherlands, an agency may not ask you money for finding you a job. Did you have to borrow money for the trip or for the job, and does the debt keep growing? Must you stay until it is paid? That is a sign of exploitation. A debt never means that you must keep working: you may stop. Keep every paper and message about the debt. General information. For your situation: ask the union, the Juridisch Loket or FairWork.
gloss.c.debt.p: How much do I still have to pay? I want it on paper.
gloss.c.debt.s: The agency paid your bus ticket. Now it takes money off your pay every week, and the debt does not get smaller. What do you do?
gloss.c.debt.o1: Ask for a list on paper, and get help.
gloss.c.debt.o2: Work more hours to pay it faster.
gloss.c.debt.o3: Say nothing: the agency helped you.
gloss.c.debt.w: A debt that does not get smaller keeps you stuck. With the list, the union or FairWork can check if it is fair.
gloss.w.inspectie: the inspection (people who check if work is fair and safe)
gloss.w.mensenhandel: human trafficking (people are used and sold for work or sex)
gloss.s.inspection.3: I do not trust this man.
gloss.c.inspection.q: Do you want to talk to the inspection?
gloss.c.inspection.a: Yes, but my boss may not hear it.
gloss.c.inspection: The inspection is there for you
gloss.c.inspection.b: The Nederlandse Arbeidsinspectie checks if work is safe and fair: pay, hours and exploitation. Inspectors may come to your work and talk to the workers. You may tell them the truth: they do not tell your boss who reported something. Need help in your own language? Ask for an interpreter. FairWork helps victims of exploitation for free, also people without valid papers. General information. For your situation: ask the union, the Juridisch Loket or FairWork.
gloss.c.inspection.p: I want to tell something, but without my boss there.
gloss.c.inspection.s: An inspector asks about your hours. Your boss told you to say 8 hours. You work 12. What do you do?
gloss.c.inspection.o2: Say 8 hours, as your boss said.
gloss.c.inspection.w: The inspector can only help when they know the truth. What you say helps you, and your colleagues too.
gloss.w.carpoolen: to carpool (drive to work together in one car)
gloss.w.meerijden: to ride along (in someone else’s car)
gloss.w.instappen: to get in (a car, a bus or a train)
gloss.w.uitstappen: to get out (of a car, a bus or a train)
gloss.s.carpool.1: May I ride along with you?
gloss.s.carpool.3: I get out at the station.
gloss.c.carpool.a: I am driving. At six I will pick you up.
gloss.c.carpool: In the car: belt on, and agree on the costs
gloss.c.carpool.b: Everyone in the car wears a seat belt, also in the back. The driver needs a valid driving licence, and should not drink alcohol before driving. Too many people in the van, or does the driver drive dangerously? Say it, and do not get in. Carpool with colleagues? Agree first how you share the fuel costs. In the work van of the agency? Ask what it costs you, and get it on paper.
gloss.c.carpool.p: There are too many people in the van. I am not getting in.
gloss.c.carpool.s: The work van has 9 seats. This morning 11 people want to get in. What do you do?
gloss.c.carpool.o1: Do not get in, and call your supervisor.
gloss.c.carpool.o2: Sit on the floor in the back.
gloss.c.carpool.o3: Squeeze in: it is only 20 minutes.
gloss.c.carpool.w: Without a seat and a belt, a small accident can be very serious. Your employer or agency can find another way.
gloss.w.perron: the platform (where you get on the train)
gloss.w.overstappen: to change (to another train or bus)
gloss.w.uitvallen: to be cancelled (the train does not go)
gloss.w.reisplanner: the journey planner (an app that shows trains and buses)
gloss.s.train.3: From which platform does the train leave?
gloss.c.train.a: My train was cancelled. I sent you a message.
gloss.c.train: Train late? Send a message at once
gloss.c.train.b: Check the journey planner before you leave: trains and buses can be late or cancelled. Is your train late? Send your supervisor a message right away, with the time you will arrive. On days with a storm or works on the line, take an earlier train. After a long delay, you can often get money back: look on the website of the train company.
gloss.c.train.p: My train is delayed. I will be there at nine.
gloss.c.train.s: Your train is cancelled. The next one goes in 30 minutes. Your shift starts in 40 minutes. What do you do?
gloss.c.train.o1: Send a message now that you will be late.
gloss.c.train.o2: Wait, and explain it when you get there.
gloss.c.train.o3: Go home: it is not your fault.
gloss.c.train.w: Your supervisor can plan better when they know early. A delay is not your fault, but telling it is your job.
gloss.w.checklist: the checklist (a list of things to check)
gloss.w.afvinken: to tick off (put a tick behind a task)
gloss.s.checklist.1: I tick off everything on the checklist.
gloss.s.checklist.3: I have to do this again.
gloss.c.checklist.a: I will look at the checklist one more time.
gloss.c.checklist.b: Before you say "klaar", check your own work. Use the checklist if there is one, and tick off each step. Look at your work as if you are the customer. Is something not good? Do it again now: that is quicker than later. Not sure? Ask a colleague to look. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.checklist.p: I am done. Will you check it for a moment?
gloss.c.checklist.s: You are done. On the checklist, one step is not ticked off. You think you did it. What do you do?
gloss.c.checklist.o1: Check that step again, then tick it off.
gloss.c.checklist.o2: Tick it off: you probably did it.
gloss.c.checklist.o3: Leave it open: nobody reads the list.
gloss.c.checklist.w: A checklist only helps when it is true. One more look takes a minute. A mistake can take hours.
gloss.w.uitdoen: to switch off (the light, a machine)
gloss.w.achterlaten: to leave behind (how you leave your place)
gloss.s.leavesite.3: Switch off the light and close the door.
gloss.c.leavesite.q: Are you the last one to leave today?
gloss.c.leavesite.a: Yes. I switch everything off and lock the door.
gloss.c.leavesite: Leave it as you want to find it
gloss.c.leavesite.b: At the end of your work, leave your place clean and safe. Put tools and materials back, and sweep the floor. Switch off the machines and lights you used. Are you the last one? Check the windows and doors, and lock up the way your company says. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.leavesite.p: I am the last one. Must I lock the door?
gloss.c.leavesite.s: You are the last one at work. You do not know how to set the alarm. What do you do?
gloss.c.leavesite.o2: Leave without the alarm: it is late.
gloss.c.leavesite.w: A building without the alarm is not safe. Your supervisor would rather get a call than find a problem tomorrow.
gloss.w.stageplek: the placement (the company where you do your placement)
gloss.w.stagevergoeding: the placement allowance (money you may get at your placement)
gloss.s.stagedays.1: I am absent tomorrow. I am sick.
gloss.s.stagedays.2: Do I get a placement allowance?
gloss.s.stagedays.3: At my placement I work four days.
gloss.c.stagedays.a: I was sick. I called the school and the company.
gloss.c.stagedays.b: At your placement you are there to learn, but you work like a colleague: on time, with the house rules, and you call when you are sick. You may ask a lot of questions: that is why you are there. Your work should help you learn, not only cleaning or carrying all day. Is that not so? Talk to your placement coach at school. A placement allowance is not always given: ask about it before you start. Rules differ per school: ask your placement coach.
gloss.c.stagedays.p: I want to learn this too. May I watch?
gloss.c.stagedays.s: At your placement you only clean the canteen, every day, for three weeks. What do you do?
gloss.c.stagedays.o1: Talk about it with your placement coach.
gloss.c.stagedays.o2: Do it and say nothing: you are a student.
gloss.c.stagedays.o3: Stay home until they give you other work.
gloss.c.stagedays.w: A placement is for learning your profession. Your coach can talk with the company about better tasks.
gloss.w.eindgesprek: the final talk (at the end of your placement)
gloss.w.trakteren: to treat (bring something nice to eat for everyone)
gloss.s.stageend.1: Tomorrow I have my final talk.
gloss.c.stageend.q: Your last day! What are you going to do now?
gloss.c.stageend.a: First get my diploma. Then I will look for work.
gloss.c.stageend: End well, and ask for a reference
gloss.c.stageend.b: In the final talk you hear what went well and what can be better. Ask for examples, and write them down for your next job. Did it go well? Ask if you may give their name as a reference. On your last day, thank your colleagues: many people here bring something small to eat, like cake or sweets. Rules differ per school: ask your placement coach.
gloss.c.stageend.p: May I give your name as a reference?
gloss.c.stageend.s: It is the last day of your placement. What do you do?
gloss.c.stageend.o1: Thank your colleagues, and say goodbye.
gloss.c.stageend.o3: Ask the company for a present.
gloss.c.stageend.w: A good goodbye leaves a good picture. Maybe you want to work there later, or you need them as a reference.
gloss.w.buurthuis: the community centre (a house for activities in your neighbourhood)
gloss.w.kennismaken: to get to know (meet someone for the first time)
gloss.w.overlast: the nuisance (noise or trouble for others)
gloss.s.neighbours.1: I have lived in this street for a short time.
gloss.s.neighbours.2: In the library I practise Dutch.
gloss.c.neighbours.q: Hello, I am your new neighbour.
gloss.c.neighbours.a: Nice to meet you! I am Ali.
gloss.c.neighbours.b: New in a street? Say hello to your neighbours and tell them your name. That makes problems easier to solve later. Work nights, or do you live with many people? Keep it quiet late in the evening and at night. Put your rubbish out on the right day. In the library and the community centre you can often practise Dutch, sometimes for free.
gloss.c.neighbours.p: Hello, I am Ali. I live next door.
gloss.c.neighbours.s: You live with five colleagues. A neighbour says it is often noisy at night. What do you do?
gloss.c.neighbours.o1: Say sorry, and agree to keep it quiet.
gloss.c.neighbours.o2: Say that you all work and need to relax.
gloss.c.neighbours.o3: Say nothing, and close the door.
gloss.c.neighbours.w: A good talk early stops bigger problems. Neighbours who know you are often friendlier and more helpful.
gloss.w.vrijwilliger: the volunteer (someone who helps without pay)
gloss.s.join.1: My son goes to primary school.
gloss.s.join.2: I play football at a sports club.
gloss.s.join.3: On Saturday I do volunteer work.
gloss.c.join.q: Are you coming to the parents’ evening?
gloss.c.join.a: Yes. I would like to talk to the teacher.
gloss.c.join: Join in: you learn Dutch faster
gloss.c.join.b: Outside work, you learn Dutch fastest by doing things with people: sports, a club, or volunteer work. Your child at school? Go to the parents’ evening, also if your Dutch is not perfect: the teacher wants to meet you. You may ask for slow Dutch, or use a translation app. Volunteer work also looks good on your CV.
gloss.c.join.p: Would you speak a bit slower?
gloss.c.join.s: You are invited to the parents’ evening. Your Dutch is not good yet. What do you do?
gloss.c.join.o1: Go, and use simple Dutch or an app.
gloss.c.join.o2: Do not go: the teacher will not understand you.
gloss.c.join.o3: Send a short message that you are busy.
gloss.c.join.w: The teacher wants to talk about your child, not about your Dutch. Coming shows that you care.
gloss.w.klantgegevens: the customer details (name, address, phone of a customer)
gloss.s.workphotos.1: I do not post photos of work online.
gloss.s.workphotos.2: I delete the photo right away.
gloss.s.workphotos.3: His face is in the photo.
gloss.c.workphotos.q: May I take a photo of you? For the internet.
gloss.c.workphotos.a: No, I would rather not. I do not want to be online.
gloss.c.workphotos.b: A photo at work can show more than you think: a customer, a client, a screen or a paper with names. Do not post photos of work online without permission from your employer, and never photos of people without their yes. Customer details stay at work: do not send them to your own phone or e-mail. Sent something by mistake? Tell your supervisor right away. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.workphotos.p: I will ask for permission first.
gloss.c.workphotos.s: A colleague puts a funny photo of a customer in the team app. What do you do?
gloss.c.workphotos.o1: Say that it is not okay, and do not share it.
gloss.c.workphotos.o2: Share it: it is only in the team app.
gloss.c.workphotos.o3: Like it, but do not share it.
gloss.c.workphotos.w: The customer did not say yes to this photo. Photos in an app can go anywhere, fast. Saying it kindly protects the customer and your colleague.
gloss.w.update: the update (a new version of an app or a program)
gloss.w.virus: the virus (a program that harms your computer)
gloss.s.device.1: I am installing the update tonight.
gloss.s.device.2: This USB stick was lying on the floor.
gloss.c.device.q: May I put this app on the work phone?
gloss.c.device.b: Install the updates on your phone and computer: they close holes that hackers use. Found a USB stick? Do not put it in your computer: give it to the IT department. On a work phone or computer, only install apps that your work allows. On public wifi, do not log in to your bank or your work. Lock your phone with a code. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.device.p: I found a USB stick. What should I do with it?
gloss.c.device.s: You find a USB stick in the car park. It says "Salaris". What do you do?
gloss.c.device.o1: Give it to the IT department.
gloss.c.device.o2: Put it in your computer to see whose it is.
gloss.c.device.o3: Take it home and look at it there.
gloss.c.device.w: A stick can have a virus on it, also when it looks interesting. The IT department can check it safely.
gloss.w.vog: the certificate of conduct (VOG: a paper from the government that says your past is no problem for this job)
gloss.w.strafblad: the criminal record (the crimes a court has found you guilty of)
gloss.w.screening: the background check (a check of your past before you start)
gloss.w.personenregister: the register for child care (everyone who works in child care must be in it)
gloss.w.beveiligerspas: the security guard pass (the card you need to work as a guard)
gloss.s.vog.1: In care work they almost always ask for a VOG.
gloss.s.vog.2: I have a VOG and I am in the register for child care.
gloss.s.vog.3: I get my security guard pass after the screening.
gloss.c.vog.q: The agency asks for a VOG. Do you have one yet?
gloss.c.vog.a: No. I am still waiting for the e-mail from Justis.
gloss.w.verbodsbord: the prohibition sign (a red circle with a line through it: you may not do this)
gloss.w.gebodsbord: the mandatory sign (a blue circle with a white picture: you must do this)
gloss.w.waarschuwingsbord: the warning sign (a yellow triangle with a black edge: watch out, danger)
gloss.w.reddingsbord: the safe condition sign (a green rectangle: the way out, or first aid)
gloss.w.brandbord: the fire equipment sign (a red square: here is a fire extinguisher or a fire hose)
gloss.w.pictogram: the pictogram (a simple picture that says something without words)
gloss.s.safetysigns.1: A red round sign means: that is not allowed.
gloss.s.safetysigns.2: A blue sign says what you must do.
gloss.s.safetysigns.3: Follow the green signs to the emergency exit.
gloss.c.safetysigns.q: What does this yellow sign mean?
gloss.c.safetysigns.a: Watch out, danger. It is a warning sign.
gloss.w.stofmasker: the dust mask (it covers your nose and mouth)
gloss.w.bijtend: corrosive (it burns your skin or eats into metal)
gloss.w.opbergen: to put away (in its own place, for example a cupboard that locks)
gloss.w.dop: the cap (of a bottle or a can)
gloss.s.substances.1: First look at the hazard symbol on the label.
gloss.s.substances.2: Never pour it into a drinks bottle.
gloss.s.substances.3: You must wear a dust mask here.
gloss.c.substances.a: That is on the safety data sheet. I will look it up.
gloss.w.branddriehoek: the fire triangle (fire needs fuel, air and heat; take one away and the fire goes out)
gloss.w.zuurstof: the oxygen (in the air; fire needs it)
gloss.w.openvuur: open fire (a flame, for example from a lighter or a gas burner)
gloss.w.brandslang: the fire hose (on a reel in the wall)
gloss.s.firefight.1: Never throw water on burning oil.
gloss.s.firefight.2: You only put out a small fire yourself.
gloss.s.firefight.3: Put the fire blanket over the pan.
gloss.c.firefight.q: There is a fire in the bin!
gloss.c.firefight.a: It is small. I will get the fire extinguisher.
gloss.w.werkvergunningveilig: the permit to work (a safety paper for dangerous work: what, where and which dangers; not your residence or work papers)
gloss.w.beslotenruimte: the confined space (a tank, a pit or a sewer: small, with little fresh air)
gloss.w.gasmeting: the gas test (you measure the air before you go in)
gloss.w.mangatwacht: the hole watch (the person who stays outside at the opening, keeps contact and raises the alarm)
gloss.w.signaalgever: the banksman (the person who gives the crane driver hand signs)
gloss.w.hijsen: to lift (a load with a crane)
gloss.s.permitwork.1: We do not start without a permit to work.
gloss.s.permitwork.2: First a gas test, only then into the confined space.
gloss.s.permitwork.3: Watch the banksman: lift, lower, stop.
gloss.c.permitwork.q: Who stays outside at the tank?
gloss.c.permitwork.a: Me. I am the hole watch.
gloss.c.vog: The VOG: a check of your past
gloss.c.vog.b: For some jobs, the agency or the employer asks for a VOG (Verklaring Omtrent het Gedrag). It is a paper from the government: it says that your past is no problem for this job. In care, child care and security work you almost always need one. Usually the employer starts the request online. You get an e-mail from Justis, and you finish it with DigiD and pay. Ask first who pays: often the employer pays it back. For volunteers who work with children or vulnerable people it is often free. Do you have a record? That does not always mean no VOG: Justis looks at what matters for this job. Not sure? Ask the Juridisch Loket. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.vog.p: Must I pay for the VOG myself?
gloss.c.vog.s: Your new job in a care home asks for a VOG. Years ago, you had a problem with the police. What do you do?
gloss.c.vog.o1: Apply, and ask the Juridisch Loket if you are worried.
gloss.c.vog.o2: Do not apply: you will never get it.
gloss.c.vog.o3: Say you have no time, and look for other work.
gloss.c.vog.w: Justis only looks at what matters for the job. Many people with something in their past still get a VOG. Advice helps if you are not sure.
gloss.c.safetysigns.b: VCA is a safety certificate. Many companies, also through an agency, ask for it, for example in construction and industry. Most workers do B-VCA (VCA Basis); a supervisor does VOL-VCA. You do a course, and an exam with multiple-choice questions at a recognised exam centre. You can often do the exam in several languages, for example English or Polish: ask the exam centre. The diploma is valid for 10 years. Often the employer or the agency pays: ask before you pay yourself. An agency may not take just any cost off your pay (see the topic about agency work). In these lessons you learn some words that you meet in safe work and in VCA. For VCA you do a course and an exam. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.safetysigns.p: Who pays for the VCA course?
gloss.c.safetysigns.s: An agency says: "You need VCA. You pay the course, or we take it off your pay." What do you do?
gloss.c.safetysigns.o1: Ask who pays, and get it in writing.
gloss.c.safetysigns.o2: Pay right away, so you get the job.
gloss.c.safetysigns.w: Often the employer or the agency pays for VCA. If you must pay something, you want to know it before, on paper.
gloss.c.substances.b: A dangerous product has a red diamond on the label, with a black picture in it: the hazard symbol. The picture shows the danger, for example fire, poison, or a product that burns your skin. The label and the safety data sheet (veiligheidsblad) say how to work with it safely, and what to do if something goes wrong. Wear what they say: gloves, safety glasses or a mask. Close the cap, and put the product away in its own place. Never pour it into a drinks bottle: someone can drink it. Do not eat, drink or smoke while you work with it, and wash your hands afterwards. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.substances.p: Where is the safety data sheet for this product?
gloss.c.substances.s: A colleague pours a cleaning product into an empty water bottle, to take it with him. What do you do?
gloss.c.substances.o1: Say it is dangerous: someone can drink it.
gloss.c.substances.o2: Nothing: it is his own bottle.
gloss.c.substances.o3: Put a small sticker on the bottle.
gloss.c.substances.w: In a drinks bottle, a product looks like water or lemonade. Someone can drink it by mistake. A product stays in its own packaging, with the label.
gloss.c.firefight.b: Fire needs three things: fuel, air and heat. This is the fire triangle. Take one away, and the fire goes out. A fire blanket takes away the air. Water takes away the heat, but never use water on burning oil or fat, or on electrical things. Look at the fire extinguisher: it says what it is for. Foam and powder work on many fires; CO2 is good for electrical fires. Keep sparks and open fire away from products that burn easily. Only put out a small fire yourself, and only when it is safe. Is it bigger? Go out, close the door behind you, and raise the alarm. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.firefight.s: Oil in a pan catches fire in the canteen. The flames are still small. What do you do?
gloss.c.firefight.o1: Put the fire blanket over the pan.
gloss.c.firefight.o2: Throw a glass of water on it.
gloss.c.firefight.w: Water on burning oil makes a big ball of fire. The blanket takes away the air, and the fire goes out. Turn off the heat if you can.
gloss.c.permitwork.b: For dangerous work, like welding near things that burn, or work in a tank or a pit, the company often uses a permit to work (werkvergunning). This is a safety paper, not your residence or work papers. It says what you do, where, which dangers there are, and what to do about them. Read it, and only start when it is signed. In a confined space there can be too little air or a dangerous gas: first a gas test, and a hole watch stays outside. Is someone in trouble inside? Raise the alarm: never go in without protection. With a crane, one person gives the signs: the banksman. Never stand under a hanging load. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.permitwork.p: Is the permit to work signed yet?
gloss.c.permitwork.s: Your colleague in a tank does not answer. You are the hole watch. What do you do?
gloss.c.permitwork.o1: Raise the alarm, and stay outside.
gloss.c.permitwork.o2: Climb in quickly to help him.
gloss.c.permitwork.o3: Wait a few minutes, then look.
gloss.c.permitwork.w: The gas that hurt your colleague can hurt you too. Many victims in tanks were helpers. After the alarm, help with protection comes.
gloss.l.plantround: The round and the control room
gloss.w.controlekamer: the control room (where operators watch the whole plant on screens)
gloss.w.operator: the operator (the person who runs and watches the machines of a plant)
gloss.w.drukmeter: the pressure gauge (a round meter with a needle)
gloss.w.niveau: the level (how full a tank or a silo is)
gloss.w.snelheid: the speed (how fast a line or a machine runs)
gloss.w.alarmmelding: the alarm message (a warning on the screen that something is wrong)
gloss.c.plantround.q: Why is there an alarm on the screen?
gloss.c.plantround.a: The level in tank two is too high.
gloss.w.stilstand: the standstill (the line stops, and nothing is made)
gloss.w.opstarten: to start up (a machine or a line, step by step)
gloss.w.stilzetten: to shut down (to stop a machine the right way)
gloss.w.technischedienst: the maintenance department (the TD: they repair the machines)
gloss.w.resetten: to reset (to clear a fault on the screen or the panel)
gloss.s.plantfault.1: When there is a fault, I call the shift leader.
gloss.s.plantfault.2: Never reach into a running machine.
gloss.s.plantfault.3: The maintenance department is on its way.
gloss.c.plantfault.q: May I start up the line again?
gloss.c.plantfault.a: No, wait. The mechanic’s lock is still on it.
gloss.w.ploeg: the shift team (the group that works the same shifts)
gloss.w.ploegwissel: the shift change (one team goes home, the next team starts)
gloss.w.volcontinu: around the clock (the plant runs day and night, every day of the week)
gloss.w.overdagslapen: to sleep in the daytime (after a night shift)
gloss.w.aflosser: the relief (the colleague who takes over your place)
gloss.s.shiftwork.1: Our plant runs around the clock.
gloss.s.shiftwork.2: Write it in the logbook for the next shift team.
gloss.s.shiftwork.3: I am on time for the handover.
gloss.c.shiftwork.a: Pump three stopped. It is in the logbook.
gloss.w.smeltoven: the furnace (a very hot oven that melts glass or metal)
gloss.w.stoomleiding: the steam pipe (it is hot, also when you see no steam)
gloss.w.kwartsstof: the quartz dust (very fine dust from clay, sand or stone; it damages your lungs)
gloss.w.explosiegevaar: the danger of explosion (dust or vapour in the air can explode; a yellow sign with EX)
gloss.s.heatdust.1: Drink water often near the furnace.
gloss.s.heatdust.2: You cannot see quartz dust. Put on your dust mask.
gloss.s.heatdust.3: There is a danger of explosion here: no sparks.
gloss.c.heatdust.q: May my phone come into this zone?
gloss.c.heatdust.a: No. There is a danger of explosion here.
gloss.c.plantround: Walk your round, write it down
gloss.c.plantround.b: A plant that runs day and night needs eyes and ears. On your round you look, listen and smell: a new noise, a leak or a strange smell can be the first sign of a problem. You read the meters: the temperature, the pressure, the speed and the level. Write every value down right away, with the time, on the list or in the system. Not later, from memory. Is a value too high or too low? Tell the control room or your shift leader at once. An alarm on the screen is never "just an alarm": do not switch it off before you know why it went. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.plantround.s: On your round, the pressure is a bit too high. Your shift almost ends. What do you do?
gloss.c.plantround.o1: Tell the control room right away.
gloss.c.plantround.o2: Write it down, and tell nobody.
gloss.c.plantround.o3: Leave it for the next shift.
gloss.c.plantround.w: In a plant a small change can grow fast. When the control room knows it early, they can act before something goes wrong.
gloss.c.plantfault.b: When there is a fault, the line stops, and everyone wants it to run again fast. But many accidents happen exactly then. Never reach into a running machine, also not "just for a moment". Call your shift leader or the maintenance department. Before anyone works on the machine, it is stopped and locked, so nobody can start it. Often everyone who works on it puts their own lock on it. Only start up again when every lock is off and your shift leader says it is safe. Start up step by step, the way you learned it. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.plantfault.p: There is still a lock on it.
gloss.c.plantfault.s: A product is stuck in the machine. The machine still runs. A colleague says: "Pull it out quickly." What do you do?
gloss.c.plantfault.o1: Do not reach in: call the shift leader.
gloss.c.plantfault.o2: Pull it out quickly with your hand.
gloss.c.plantfault.o3: Push it out with a stick while it runs.
gloss.c.plantfault.w: A machine that still runs can move at any moment. A machine that is stopped and locked cannot hurt you.
gloss.c.shiftwork: Nights: sleep, eat, be on time
gloss.c.shiftwork.b: Many plants run day and night, every day of the week. You work early, late and night shifts in turn, often in three or five shift teams. After a night shift, sleep in a dark and quiet room, and tell your family when you sleep. Eat at fixed times, and take your own food: at night the canteen is often closed. Be on time for the handover: your colleague is waiting, and the plant may not be left alone. For night shifts there are extra rules, in the law and often in the cao, for example about rest after your nights. Ask what the rules are where you work. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.shiftwork.p: What are the rules for night shifts?
gloss.c.shiftwork.s: After four nights, your shift leader asks you to work one more night. You are very tired. What do you do?
gloss.c.shiftwork.o1: Say you are very tired, and ask about the rules.
gloss.c.shiftwork.o2: Say yes, and drink a lot of coffee.
gloss.c.shiftwork.o3: Say yes, and sleep a bit in your break.
gloss.c.shiftwork.w: Tired people make more mistakes, and in a plant a mistake can be dangerous. There are rules about rest after night shifts.
gloss.c.heatdust.b: Near a furnace, a kiln or steam it is very hot. Drink water often, also before you feel thirsty. Wear the heat-protective clothing, and do not touch pipes or parts without gloves: steam and hot metal burn, also when you do not see them. Do you feel dizzy or sick? Stop, go to a cool place and tell someone. Dust from clay, sand or stone can hold quartz dust (kwartsstof). You do not see it, but it damages your lungs. Use the extraction, wear your dust mask, and never blow dust away with compressed air. In some zones, dust or vapour can explode: a yellow sign with EX shows it. There: no sparks, no fire, and often no normal phone. Ask what is allowed in each zone. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.heatdust.p: I do not feel well. I am going to a cool place.
gloss.c.heatdust.s: There is fine clay dust on your machine. A colleague says: "Blow it off with the air gun." What do you do?
gloss.c.heatdust.o1: Clean it wet, or with the vacuum.
gloss.c.heatdust.o2: Blow it off: it is faster.
gloss.c.heatdust.o3: Leave it for the next shift.
gloss.c.heatdust.w: Blowing makes the dust fly up, into the air and into your lungs. A wet cloth or a vacuum keeps the dust down.
gloss.w.herinnering: the reminder (a letter: you have not paid yet)
gloss.w.aanmaning: the final reminder (pay before a date, or extra costs may come)
gloss.w.betalingsregeling: the payment plan (you pay a debt in small parts)
gloss.w.deurwaarder: the bailiff (an official who collects a debt, often after a judge has decided)
gloss.w.schuldhulp: the debt help (free help with your debts, from the town council)
gloss.w.achterstand: the arrears (money you should have paid already)
gloss.s.debthelp.3: I want help with my debts.
gloss.c.debthelp.q: You have not paid the bill yet.
gloss.c.debthelp.a: That is right. May I have a payment plan?
gloss.w.jaaropgave: the annual statement (a paper from your employer with your pay of the whole year)
gloss.w.blauweenvelop: the blue envelope (letters from the Belastingdienst come in it)
gloss.w.teruggave: the refund (tax money you get back)
gloss.w.uitstel: the extra time (you may do it later)
gloss.w.huurtoeslag: the rent benefit (money from the government to help you pay the rent)
gloss.w.belastingtelefoon: the free phone line of the Belastingdienst
gloss.s.taxes.1: I need my annual statement for the tax return.
gloss.s.taxes.2: I earn more now. I pass that on right away.
gloss.s.taxes.3: I am getting money back from the Belastingdienst.
gloss.c.taxes.q: There is a blue envelope for you.
gloss.c.taxes.a: Thank you. I will open it right away.
gloss.w.afkomst: the origin (the country or the group you or your family come from)
gloss.w.uitschelden: to call someone names (to say ugly words to someone)
gloss.w.bedreigen: to threaten (to say you will hurt someone)
gloss.s.discrimination.1: I am treated differently because of my religion.
gloss.s.discrimination.2: He is threatening me. I do not feel safe.
gloss.s.discrimination.3: I may say no, also to my boss.
gloss.c.discrimination.q: Are you okay? They keep calling you names.
gloss.c.discrimination.a: No, I am not okay. I am going to report it.
gloss.l.union: The union and the works council
gloss.w.lidworden: to join, to become a member
gloss.w.contributie: the membership fee (you pay it every month)
gloss.w.opkomenvoor: to stand up for (to defend someone’s interests)
gloss.w.onderhandelen: to negotiate (to talk until both sides agree)
gloss.w.ondernemingsraad: the works council (the OR: colleagues chosen to talk with the director)
gloss.s.union.2: The union negotiates about the cao.
gloss.s.union.3: Who is on the works council?
gloss.c.union.q: Why are you a member of the union?
gloss.c.union.a: They stand up for me when there is a problem.
gloss.w.pers: the press (a machine that presses clay or powder into a shape)
gloss.w.glazuur: the glaze (a shiny, glassy layer on a tile or a cup)
gloss.w.tunneloven: the tunnel kiln (a long oven; the products ride slowly through it)
gloss.w.scherf: the shard (a sharp piece of broken glass or tile)
gloss.w.gloeiend: glowing hot (so hot that it shines red)
gloss.w.armbeschermer: the arm guard (a sleeve that protects your arm against cuts)
gloss.s.kiln.1: The tiles go slowly through the tunnel kiln.
gloss.s.kiln.2: There is a crack in this tile. It is a reject.
gloss.s.kiln.3: Wear your arm guards near the glass.
gloss.c.kiln.q: May I pick up the shards with my hand?
gloss.c.kiln.a: No. Use a brush and dustpan.
gloss.l.mixlab: The mixing hall and the lab
gloss.w.batch: the batch (one amount that is made at once, by one recipe)
gloss.w.afwegen: to weigh out (to weigh exactly as much as the recipe says)
gloss.w.mengvat: the mixing tank (a big tank with a mixer in it)
gloss.w.laboratorium: the laboratory (the lab: here they test the product)
gloss.w.grondstof: the raw material (what you make the product from)
gloss.s.mixlab.1: Weigh out the raw materials exactly.
gloss.s.mixlab.2: I am taking a sample for the lab.
gloss.s.mixlab.3: Which batch is this? Look at the label.
gloss.c.mixlab.a: Not yet. The lab is testing the sample.
gloss.c.debthelp: Open every letter, and ask for help early
gloss.c.debthelp.b: Did you not pay a bill in time? Then you first get a reminder (herinnering), and later a final reminder (aanmaning). Before a company may charge you extra costs for this, it must give you 14 days to pay. So open every letter, also when you are afraid of it. Cannot pay all at once? Call or write, and ask for a payment plan (betalingsregeling). A deurwaarder (bailiff) is an official who collects debts, often after a judge has decided. He can, for example, take part of your pay, but he must always leave you enough to live on. Debts? Ask for help early, when they are still small. The gemeente gives free debt help (schuldhulp). On geldfit.nl you can do a free test and find help near you. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.debthelp.p: I cannot pay everything at once. Can I pay in parts?
gloss.c.debthelp.s: You get a final reminder for your phone bill. You do not have the money this month. What do you do?
gloss.c.debthelp.o1: Call the company, and ask for a payment plan.
gloss.c.debthelp.o2: Put the letter away, and wait.
gloss.c.debthelp.o3: Borrow money quickly with buy now, pay later.
gloss.c.debthelp.w: When you say it in time, the company can often agree on small payments. A letter you put away does not go away: the costs only grow.
gloss.c.taxes: Your tax return and your allowances
gloss.c.taxes.b: The tax return (aangifte) for last year must be done before 1 May. Did you get a letter that asks you to do it? Then you must. Sometimes you get money back. You need the annual statement (jaaropgave) from your employer. No time? You can ask for more time (uitstel). Allowances (toeslagen), like zorgtoeslag and huurtoeslag, are an advance: they depend on what you will earn this year. Do you earn more, or does something else change? Pass it on right away in Mijn toeslagen. If you do not, you may have to pay a lot back later. Must you pay back? You can ask for a payment plan. Free help: the BelastingTelefoon, a Belastingdienst office (make an appointment first) or the library. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.taxes.p: My income has changed. How do I pass that on?
gloss.c.taxes.s: You get a new job and earn more each month. You get huurtoeslag. What do you do?
gloss.c.taxes.o1: Pass on your new income in Mijn toeslagen.
gloss.c.taxes.w: Your allowance is based on what you earn. When you pass on the change in time, you get the right amount, and you do not have to pay a lot back later.
gloss.c.discrimination: Treated unfairly? It is not your fault
gloss.c.discrimination.b: Discrimination is when you are treated differently or worse because of who you are: your origin, skin colour, religion, gender, age, a disability or who you love. Intimidation is, for example, unwanted touching, sexual remarks, threats or calling you names. Both are not allowed at work, and it is never your fault. You may say no, also to your boss. Write down what happened, when, and who saw it. Talk to your supervisor, or to the vertrouwenspersoon if your company has one. Outside your work, the anti-discrimination service in your town helps for free (discriminatie.nl). The College voor de Rechten van de Mens can give a judgement, also for free. Violence or a threat? Go to the police. In danger: call 112. General information. For your situation: ask the union, the Juridisch Loket or FairWork.
gloss.c.discrimination.p: I want to report something. Can I talk to you in confidence?
gloss.c.discrimination.s: A colleague often calls you names because of where you come from. Others laugh. What do you do?
gloss.c.discrimination.o1: Write it down, and tell someone you trust.
gloss.c.discrimination.o2: Say nothing: it is part of the job.
gloss.c.discrimination.w: Calling names because of your origin is discrimination, and it is not allowed. When you write it down and talk about it, someone can help you make it stop.
gloss.c.union.b: A union (vakbond), for example FNV or CNV, stands up for workers. It makes agreements with employers about pay and work: the cao. Many cao’s count for everyone in a sector, also when you are not a member. Members pay a fee (contributie) every month, and get advice and help, for example with a problem about pay or dismissal. Join in time: often the union only helps with a problem that starts after you join. Joining is your own choice, and your employer may not punish you for it. A company with 50 or more workers must have a works council (ondernemingsraad, OR): colleagues chosen by the workers. The OR talks with the director about, for example, working hours and safety. A smaller company can have a staff council (personeelsvertegenwoordiging). Questions? Ask a colleague in the OR. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.union.p: I have a question about the new rosters. Can the OR do something with it?
gloss.c.union.s: Your company plans many more evening shifts. Many colleagues are unhappy. What can you do?
gloss.c.union.o1: Ask a colleague in the OR about it.
gloss.c.union.w: The OR has a say in rules about working hours. It can talk about them with the director, for all the workers together.
gloss.c.kiln.b: In a tile or glass plant, the products are pressed into a shape, get a glaze, and go slowly through a long kiln. After the kiln they must cool down: do not touch them while they are hot, or wear heat-resistant gloves. Glass and broken tiles are very sharp. Wear cut-resistant gloves, arm guards and safety glasses. Never catch a falling glass plate: step back. Pick up shards with a brush and dustpan, never with your hands, and put them in the right bin. Glaze and dust can hold harmful substances: wash your hands before you eat or drink. At the press, never reach in while it runs. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.kiln.p: Watch out, shards! I will get a brush and dustpan.
gloss.c.kiln.s: A glass plate slips out of the rack and starts to fall. What do you do?
gloss.c.kiln.o1: Step back, and let it fall.
gloss.c.kiln.w: A falling plate can cut very deep, also through gloves. A broken plate only costs money.
gloss.c.mixlab.b: In a mixing hall you make a batch by a recipe: which raw materials, how much, and in which order. Weigh everything exactly, and write down what you added, with the batch number. Not sure? Ask, do not guess. Before you use a drum or a bag, read the label: what is in it, the batch number and the danger signs. Never put something in a drum or a bag that does not belong in it. For a sample, use a clean scoop and a clean pot, and put a label on it at once. Powder and vapour can be harmful: use the extraction, and wear what is needed, like a lab coat, goggles, gloves or a mask. In food you also wear a hairnet and wash your hands often. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.mixlab.p: I am not sure. How much must go in?
gloss.c.mixlab.s: The recipe says 25 kilo. By mistake you put in 26 kilo, and it is already in the mixing tank. What do you do?
gloss.c.mixlab.o1: Tell your shift leader, and write it down.
gloss.c.mixlab.o2: Say nothing: one kilo is not much.
gloss.c.mixlab.w: One wrong amount can spoil the whole batch. When the shift leader knows it in time, the lab can check it before the batch goes on.
